attachments.document_title: Letter or message dismissing with immediate effect
attachments.label: A1
must_show: that employment ends with immediate effect
attachments.text:
Mr Ben Moser
Hofackerstrasse 36
1004 Lausanne

Lausanne, 5 June 2026

Dismissal with immediate effect

Dear Mr Moser

We hereby terminate your employment with immediate effect.

Please hand in your keys, your work phone and your depot pass today. Your final salary statement will be sent to you by post. Any personal belongings still in your locker can be collected by arrangement.

Handed over in person on 5 June 2026.

attachments.document_title: Proof of earnings from other work since the dismissal
attachments.label: A2
attachments.text:
Confirmation of payment

I, Clara Brunner, Lausanne, confirm that Mr Ben Moser, Hofackerstrasse 36, Lausanne, has carried out renovation work in my flat (painting, laying floors, removal of old furniture) at an hourly rate of CHF 30.

Amounts paid to Mr Moser:
first payment: CHF 900.00
second payment: CHF 1,280.00
Total paid: CHF 2,180.00

Paid in cash against receipt.

Clara Brunner
(signature)

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the immediate dismissal in writing?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Was the employment relationship agreed for a fixed term, with an agreed end date, rather than for an unlimited period?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the employer give as the cause of the dismissal the employee's absence from work, and does the employee say they were prevented from working through no fault of their own (for instance illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Did the employer end the employment relationship with immediate effect, without a notice period?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Has the employee earned income from other work during the time the notice period or the agreed term would still have run?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

text:
Hello,

I was dismissed on the spot by the Ahornweid Cooperative in Lausanne on 5 June 2026. Julia Meier, the cooperative's administrator, met me at the door of the depot that morning, gave me a letter and told me my employment was over with immediate effect. I wasn't even allowed to finish the shift.

I couldn't afford to sit at home, so from 15 June I started helping Clara Brunner, who lives near me, with renovating her flat: painting, flooring, carrying things. She has paid me CHF 2,180 so far. I'd rather you hear it from me.

My job at the cooperative was a normal permanent one. I've been there since August 2023 and there was never any end date in my contract.

I didn't ask Ms Meier or anyone else to give me the reasons in writing. Honestly, I was too shocked that day, and afterwards I didn't see the point.

I've attached the letter I was handed that morning, and a confirmation from Ms Brunner of what she has paid me.

My wage at the cooperative was CHF 2,800 a month. Is there anything I can claim from them? I've heard that being sacked without notice is only allowed in serious cases, and I really don't think I did anything serious.

Thank you for your help,
Ben Moser
Hofackerstrasse 36, Lausanne
